c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: How much of the black line can the car actually see at any moment?

B.text: The next few centimeters of it

c1.why: Two probes, two spots. Everything the car knows about the track comes from those two readings.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: The left probe is off the line and the right one is on it. Where has the car drifted?

B.text: It has left the track completely

C.text: It has drifted left of the line

D.text: It has drifted right of the line

c2.why: If the line has slipped over to the right-hand probe, the car itself has wandered to the left of it.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: Two probes give how many different combinations?
c3.why: Each probe is on or off, so 2 × 2 = 4: both on, left only, right only, neither.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: Both probes are on the line. What does the car do?
r1.why: Equal speeds are a straight line — and both probes on the line means there is nothing to correct.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: Which way does the car steer when this branch runs?
r2.why: The left wheel runs faster, so the car swings towards the slower right side — back towards the line it drifted away from.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: The car is following a gentle curve. What is it doing as it goes?

A.text: Driving straight and stopping to correct

B.text: Correcting constantly while it keeps moving

C.text: Waiting until it is centered before moving

D.text: Turning in place at each bend

r3.why: It never stops to think. Every trip round the loop reads the probes and nudges the wheels — that constant nudging is line following.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: How will this car behave on the track compared with using 50 and 25?

B.text: It will swing wildly past the line each time

r4.why: A huge speed difference is a hard turn. The car overshoots, the other probe catches the line, and it slams back the other way.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: The car corrects one way but leaves the line on the other side. Which change fixes it?
d1.why: Both branches steer the same way, so one drift is never corrected. The two corrections have to be mirror images.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: The car lurches off the track at every bend. What is causing it?

C.text: The one-second pauses stop it reading the probes

D.text: There is no branch for both probes on the line

d2.why: During a pause the car keeps steering blind for a whole second. Corrections have to be small and constant, not held.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Which combination should drive the car straight ahead?
b1.why: Both probes on the line means the car is sitting where it should be — nothing to correct.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: You are writing the three branches. What should each one contain?

A.text: Two motor blocks, one for each wheel

B.text: One `if` and one motor block for that combination

b2.why: A combination and its correction. One motor block already carries both wheel speeds.
